candidates.label: Egypt (Roman province, label point)
candidates.support: Egypt's identity as the Roman province along the Nile is undisputed. The label point is Wikidata's point for the province, in the desert east of the Nile valley and far from the project's other pins. Pleiades' entry for the province has no location of its own; its representative point is Alexandria, about 410 km to the northwest.

summary.text: Egypt was a Roman province governed from Alexandria under an unusual arrangement: the Roman historian Cassius Dio records that Augustus put it under its first prefect, Cornelius Gallus, rather than a senator and, because of its grain and wealth, let no senator even live there without his personal permission. In Matthew's account an angel tells Joseph to flee into Egypt with the child and his mother, because Herod will seek to destroy the child, and at Pentecost the crowd in Jerusalem includes people 'from Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, Asia, Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, the parts of Libya around Cyrene.'

history.text: After his victory over the Roman general Antony and Cleopatra, the queen of Egypt, Augustus made Egypt pay tribute and put it under Cornelius Gallus, not a senator. Cassius Dio explains that because the country was populous, volatile, and rich in grain and money, Augustus would not let any senator even live there without his personal permission.

The Roman historian Tacitus records that when the Roman general Germanicus visited Egypt in AD 19, Tiberius rebuked him sharply for entering Alexandria without imperial consent. Augustus had made it a rule of his power that no senator or leading knight could enter the country without permission, so that no one who seized the province and its approaches by land and sea could starve Italy. Writing of AD 69, Tacitus adds that Roman knights had governed Egypt in place of its former kings ever since Augustus, so the arrangement still held at this project's about AD 50 date.

scripture.textWEB: Now when they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, “Arise and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and stay there until I tell you, for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.”

otConnections.note: Matthew 2:15 applies the prophet's words 'Out of Egypt I called my son' to the family's stay in Egypt until Herod's death; in Hosea 11:1 God says he 'called my son out of Egypt.'

politicalHistory.entity: Roman Egypt (special imperial prefecture) (ruler: Equestrian prefect; senators barred without the emperor's leave)
politicalHistory.note: Suetonius: after Cleopatra's death, Augustus "reduced Egypt to the form of a province."
